fields.description:
# DC's comment ceiling is admin-configurable and rebar hardcodes the default

## The defect

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` `sanitize_comment` truncates comment bodies at
`WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767), a compile-time constant. On Jira Data Center that ceiling is the
default of the admin-settable property `jira.text.field.character.limit`, whose documented range is
`0` (unlimited) to `2147483647`.

So on an instance where an administrator has RAISED the limit or set it to `0`, rebar truncates
comments that Jira would have accepted in full. **That is data loss, and it is silent to the author
of the comment** — the operator sees a truncation warning
(`jira_family/sanitizers.py:143-148`), which is why this is low-severity rather than invisible, but
the text is still gone from the remote and the local/remote bodies then differ permanently.

This is NOT the "32767 is the wrong number" defect that was originally suspected and is now refuted
(see below). It is narrower: the number is right for a STOCK instance and wrong for a CONFIGURED one.

## Established provenance (so nobody re-litigates the number)

`jira.text.field.character.limit`, from Jira's own `jpm.xml`:

    description: "The maximum number of characters to be entered for a single field.
                  Affects Description, Environment, Comments and Text custom fields.
                  0 means unlimited."
    default-value: 32767

Corroborated by JRASERVER-28519 (Resolved/Fixed, fix versions 6.4.1 / 7.0.0): "starting with JIRA
7.0 and Cloud, `jira.text.field.character.limit` will be set to 32767 by default." The DC admin page
"Configuring advanced settings" confirms the property, its field scope, `0` = unlimited and the
2147483647 maximum, but does NOT state the default.

Comments and text custom fields share ONE property and therefore one number, by design — so binding
DC's comment limit to the same constant as its description limit is structurally faithful to DC, and
must not be "fixed" by inventing a separate comment number.

Evidence the ceiling bites people in practice: JRASERVER-64351 has 86 votes from users hitting it,
which is also the population most likely to have raised the limit.

## Why the fix is not simply "read the limit"

`/rest/api/2/application-properties` plausibly exposes the key, but **whether it is readable by a
non-admin PAT is NOT established and must be tested, not assumed.** rebar authenticates as an
ordinary user on DC. If the property is admin-only, discovery is unavailable and the remedy is
configuration only.

## Proposed remediation, cheapest first

1. Make the DC comment ceiling CONFIGURABLE, defaulting to 32767. This alone closes the data-loss
   window for any operator who knows their instance's setting.
2. OPTIONALLY probe `application-properties` at connect time and log a warning when the instance's
   value disagrees with the configured one. Gate this on actually confirming the endpoint is readable
   by rebar's credential.
3. Do NOT change the default. It is correct for stock Jira >= 7.0 and matches every independent
   implementation surveyed (carrier-io/dusty annotates its own 32767 as "the
   jira.text.field.character.limit default value").

No surveyed OSS integration queries the live limit — all hardcode — so (1) brings rebar to parity
with the field and (2) would make it more correct than the field.

## Two latent traps worth fixing in the same area (not themselves data loss today)

* The constant is named `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` and the comment at `jira_family/rich_text.py:56-60`
  attributes the number to Cloud comment limits, which REVERSES the actual causality. Renaming it
  and citing the property would stop the code asserting a false provenance.
* `sanitize_comment` reuses `fit_outbound`, the DESCRIPTION fitter. Harmless today (plain character
  truncation) but Cloud shows why the coupling is dangerous: Cloud's description fitter is
  ADF-SIZE-based (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` = 32000 ADF chars, fitted empirically because
  `text_to_adf` inflates — a 32767-char description was observed serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars)
  and would be catastrophically wrong applied to comments. Any future change to the DC description
  fitter silently retargets comments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] the DC comment ceiling is settable by configuration, defaulting to 32767, with the default's
      provenance (`jira.text.field.character.limit` + JRASERVER-28519) cited at the binding
- [x] a comment longer than the configured ceiling but shorter than a raised one is NOT truncated
      when the ceiling is configured upward, proven by a RED-first unit test
- [x] the readability of `/rest/api/2/application-properties` by rebar's non-admin PAT is RECORDED
      WITH ITS EVIDENTIARY STATUS LABELLED, discovery is dropped, and that is stated at the binding.
      **AMENDED — the original wording required an EMPIRICAL determination and the answer obtained is
      DOCUMENTARY** (Atlassian's permission documentation for the `/advanced-settings` sub-resource,
      where `jira.text.field.character.limit` is exposed). No 403 was captured, because the
      `tests/external/live_jira_dc` harness image is linux/amd64 only and never became usable on the
      arm64 host in three measured attempts. The amendment is justified on two grounds recorded in
      full in this ticket's AC-verification comment: (1) the remedy is INDEPENDENT of the answer — a
      readable endpoint would enable an OPTIONAL auto-discovery layer ON TOP of the config key, never
      a replacement, so the outstanding measurement cannot invalidate what landed; (2) the
      measurement is DEFERRED, not dropped — it is runnable on the amd64 `jira-dc-harness` CI job and
      is filed as [rebar:275e-81a4-f11a-4b5b] (linked `discovered_from` here), which writes its
      outcome back onto this ticket
- [x] `sanitize_comment` no longer depends on the description fitter, so a change to description
      fitting cannot retarget comments
- [x] mutation-checked: reverting the configurability turns the new test red for the right reason
